definitions.explanation: Clothing worn for manual labor, factory work, construction, or other hands-on jobs. Typically durable, functional garments designed to withstand dirt and physical activity. Includes coveralls, jumpsuits, and other protective workwear.

examples.japanese: {作業着|さぎょうぎ}に{着替|きが}える。
{作業着|さぎょうぎ}が{油|あぶら}で{汚|よご}れてしまった。
examples.english: My work clothes got stained with oil.

examples.japanese: {工場|こうじょう}では{全員|ぜんいん}{指定|してい}の{作業着|さぎょうぎ}を{着用|ちゃくよう}しなければならない。
examples.english: At the factory, everyone must wear the designated work uniform.

notes:
Compound of {作業|さぎょう} ('work; labor') and {着|ぎ} ('clothing; garment'). The suffix {着|ぎ} appears in many clothing compounds: {上着|うわぎ} ('jacket'), {下着|したぎ} ('underwear'), {寝巻|ねま}き ('nightwear'). Also sometimes read さぎょうふく when written {作業服|さぎょうふく}, though {作業着|さぎょうぎ} is the more common spoken form.

USAGE:
- In Japanese workplaces, changing into and out of {作業着|さぎょうぎ} is a daily ritual that marks the transition between personal time and work time.
- Many companies provide branded {作業着|さぎょうぎ} with the company logo.
- The term covers everything from light cotton work shirts to heavy-duty protective coveralls.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {作業着|さぎょうぎ}に{着替|きが}える: to change into work clothes
- {作業着|さぎょうぎ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ: to take off work clothes
- {作業着|さぎょうぎ}{姿|すがた}: appearance in work clothes
- {汚|よご}れた{作業着|さぎょうぎ}: dirty work clothes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {作業服|さぎょうふく}: work clothes — near-synonym using the {服|ふく} suffix; slightly more formal
- {制服|せいふく}: uniform — a broader term for any official uniform, not limited to manual labor
- {防護服|ぼうごふく}: protective clothing — specialized gear for hazardous environments
